newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan snubs Israel's Netanyahu after water row.
newsitem.headline: Jordan snubs Israel's Netanyahu after water row.

text.p: Jordan said it called off a meeting between Crown Prince Hassan and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday after disagreements over water supplies promised to the parched Arab kingdom under a 1994 peace treaty.

Information Minister Samir Mutawae said the prince and the prime minister had been due to hold talks during a ceremony for seven Israeli girls killed by a Jordanian soldier near their joint border in March.

But he said Israel backed out at the last minute from an accord to fulfil its peace treaty pledge to help Jordan, facing growing water shortages, to find an extra 50 million cubic metres of water a year.

Israel cancelled the whole memorial ceremony in the wake of Prince Hassan's decision to stay away. The row cast a shadow over relations between Israel and Jordan, which has forged close ties with the Jewish state in the last three years.

"I don't like to use the word crisis. But there are differences," Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali said. He said Israel should fully implement its peace treaty with Jordan if it wanted to see improved relations.

"This subject of providing the 50 million cubic metres (of water) was discussed several times in the past years," Mutawae told Reuters. "The Israelis responded by showing readiness to provide the quantity from their sources, and an understanding of Jordan's need to build dams and other collecting facilities."
The peace treaty, ending a 46-year state of war, specified that within a year of its coming into force in November 1994 the two sides would develop a plan to supply Jordan with the water.
Ideas for the water supply included desalination plants, dam building, and steps to ease pollution of river waters.
But no such plan was formally implemented.

Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh spoke earlier this week of a "frustration in the whole peace process" and said Israel's failure to follow up its commitment to help find water supplies for Jordan was a breach of the 1994 treaty.

Mutawae said Jordan thought that "a provision" for the 50 million cubic metres could be signed at the same time as the memorial ceremony for the seven Israeli schoolgirls, killed in the bloodiest border shooting for years.
"At the last minute they said they wanted the cabinet to discuss it and they were not ready to sign it," he added.

Instead of meeting Netanyahu, Prince Hassan on Tuesday held talks with Israel's opposition Labour Party member Yossi Beilin, an architect of the troubled Palestinian self-rule accord agreed with Israel in 1993.
Beilin was touting an initiative to revive talks with the Palestinians but Netanyahu's spokesmen say Beilin has no authority to conduct negotiations for Israel.

"They listened to it. They didn't have any specific remarks," Beilin said after separate talks with the prince and Majali. "They would like to see the implementation of such a plan if it is bringing about a resumption of talks between Israel and the Palestinians."
"We agreed that the point in which the peace process is now is perhaps the lowest one but there is still hope as long as we talk to each other."
The ceremony in memory of the March 13 killing was to have been held at a Jordanian beauty spot leased to Israeli farmers and known in Israel as the Island of Peace.
The girls parents were to dedicate a "hill of flowers" and plant trees at the site on Tuesday.
Jordan's King Hussein paid a condolence call on the victims' families after the attack and expressed shame at the massacre.

Netanyahu's media adviser David Bar-Illan had told Israel Radio on Monday issues to be discussed at the meeting included building a joint airport on the Red Sea, diverting Jordan River water to Jordan, tourism projects at the Dead Sea and other industry and trade issues.
